title: MILO Marathon 2026 Tagbilaran Leg Review: What the 2024 Race Was Like
seo_title: MILO Marathon Tagbilaran Review: Cut-offs, Times, Weather
meta_description: National MILO Marathon Tagbilaran leg review from 29 September 2024: a small, quick field, a 2:30 half-marathon cut-off, a 2:04 median, and 27.5°C at the 4.30am start.
dek: What the 29 September 2024 Tagbilaran leg of the National MILO Marathon was like: the pre-dawn starts, the strict MILO cut-offs, a warm, breezy Bohol morning, and a small field that runs quickly.
verdict: Enter if you want a small, quick MILO qualifier and can run a half marathon well inside 2 hours 30. The 2024 Tagbilaran leg timed only 96 half-marathon and 108 10 km finishers, so you will run much of it alone, and the field is fast: the median half took 2:04, four in ten broke 2 hours, and just one finisher was outside 2:30. The MILO rules are strict, with a 2.5-hour half-marathon cut-off and a 10 km checkpoint at 1 hour 30. Expect warm air from the gun: 27.5°C with 83% humidity at 4.30am, eased a little by a steady breeze.

sections.heading: The Race: Pre-dawn Starts and MILO Rules
paragraphs: The Tagbilaran leg is Bohol's regional qualifier in the National MILO Marathon, organised by RUNRIO. The 2024 race ran on Sunday 29 September 2024 in Tagbilaran City [1]. Its timed results cover a half marathon and a 10 km [2], with shorter fun-run distances alongside.

Under the 2024 rules the half marathon set off at 4.30am and the 10 km at 5am [1]. Winners are decided on gun time, and a runner who starts more than 10 minutes after their flag-off is disqualified [1].

sections.heading: The Weather: Warm From the Start
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's historical record for Tagbilaran shows 27.5°C at 4am and 5am on race day, with a dew point of 24.4°C and 83% humidity [3]. There was little relief before dawn, only 27.4°C at 6am, but a steady breeze of 11 to 13 km/h. After sunrise it reached 28.2°C at 7am and 29°C at 8am [3].
The air barely cooled overnight, and a dew point above 24°C makes it hard to cool by sweating. Start conservatively and drink early.

sections.heading: Cut-offs and Finisher Items
paragraphs: The MILO cut-offs are tight and enforced. The half marathon closes after 2 hours 30 and the 10 km after 1 hour 30, both counted from when the last runner crosses the start line. Half marathoners must also reach 10 km within 1 hour 30; anyone who misses a limit has to board the official vehicle and is disqualified [1].

In 2024 only one of the 96 timed half-marathon finishers was slower than 2:30, while 9 of the 108 10 km finishers took longer than 1:30 [2]. Every half-marathon finisher gets a loot bag and finisher's shirt, but the medal and certificate go only to those inside the cut-off; 10 km runners get a medal only inside the cut-off [1].
The half marathon is for runners 18 and over and needs a Fit-To-Run medical certificate signed by a doctor within two months of race day; the 10 km is for 16 and over [1].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The field is small and quick. The 2024 race timed 96 half-marathon finishers: the median ran 2:03:35, 39.6% broke 2 hours, and the slowest 10% took 2:23:11 or longer [2]. The top ten ran from 1:12:42 to 1:39:51, the fastest woman ran 1:22:59, and women were only 14.7% of the field [2].

The 10 km had 108 timed finishers, a median of 1:15:01, 16.7% under an hour and a top ten from 40:45 to 56:06; about half its finishers were women [2]. With fields this size, a sub-1:40 half marathon was a top-ten finish, and the top man and woman are eligible for an all-expenses trip to the National Finals [1].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Race kits are claimed in person, with the schedule and venue announced at least two weeks before the race. There is a baggage area for the 10 km and half marathon only, and the official MILO singlet and race number must be worn [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the Next Tagbilaran Leg?
paragraphs: Yes, if you are a solid half marathoner chasing a placing or a National Finals spot: in 2024 a sub-1:40 was a top-ten time, and the small field gives a real chance.

Think twice if you need company or a forgiving cut-off. With under a hundred half marathoners the field spreads out early, and the warm, humid start punishes anyone racing on the edge of 2:30. The 10 km is the gentler option.
The 2026 MILO calendar put the Tagbilaran leg on 13 September 2026 [4]. Check the next leg's date, start times and cut-offs on the MILO entry page before booking.
This review draws on the 2024 race rules, the official results, and historical weather records for Tagbilaran.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at the MILO Marathon Tagbilaran leg?
faqs.answer: Tight. Under the 2024 rules the half marathon closes after 2 hours 30, with 10 km to be reached in 1 hour 30, and the 10 km closes after 1 hour 30, all counted from when the last runner crosses the start. Runners who miss a limit are disqualified. In 2024 only one half-marathon finisher was slower than 2:30.

faqs.question: How big and how fast is the MILO Tagbilaran field?
faqs.answer: Small and quick. The September 2024 race timed 96 half-marathon and 108 10 km finishers. The median half took 2:03:35, 39.6% broke 2 hours, and a sub-1:40 was a top-ten finish. The 10 km median was 1:15:01. The 2026 leg was scheduled for 13 September, according to the series calendar.

faqs.question: How hot is the MILO Marathon in Tagbilaran?
faqs.answer: Warm from the gun. On race morning in September 2024 historical records for Tagbilaran show 27.5°C with a dew point of 24.4°C and 83% humidity at the 4.30am half-marathon start, with a steady breeze of about 13 km/h. It was 28.2°C by 7am and 29°C by 8am.
